text:
Quinton Byfield reached 200 career points this week, and at 24 he has a bigger job in Los Angeles: he's on the ice for 81% of the Kings' power-play chances, up from 44% last season, and his own chances are up to 1.18 expected goals per 60 (a measure of chance quality) from 0.82.

The points haven't followed. He has nine in 20 games, and the main reason is the finishing around him: the Kings have scored 10.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His play has been good. At even strength, Los Angeles takes 54.32% of the expected goals with him out there, 6.14 points better than without, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season too, 90th percentile among forwards. He also has top-end speed, 94th percentile. Our numbers project 25 goals and 46 points. That on-ice gap usually swings back, and when it does the points should catch up with the player.
headline: Quinton Byfield's points are behind his play
